title: Fed Minutes Show Officials Flagging AI Boom and High Valuations as Stability Risks
excerpt: Policymakers at the October 27-28 meeting named elevated valuations, hedge fund leverage and opaque AI financing among the system's biggest vulnerabilities, even as staff called the system resilient.
body:
• Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, released Wednesday, show officials naming elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage among the most significant financial stability risks.
  • Policymakers worried that returns on AI investment could disappoint, that AI-related debt is growing through complex and opaque financing structures, and that exposure is concentrated in a few companies.
  • The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in October; almost all officials saw further increases as possible if the economy evolves as expected, and the next decision lands at the December 8-9 meeting.
  • For investors, the message is two-sided: Fed staff called the financial system resilient, but the AI trade now carries an explicit stability warning from the central bank.

Federal Reserve officials used their October 27-28 policy meeting to put the AI investment boom near the top of the financial stability risk list, according to minutes released on Wednesday and reported by Reuters. Policymakers said elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were among the most significant sources of risk, and they worried that returns on the technology boom could fall short of what investors now expect.

The concern, as the minutes record it, runs through three channels. AI-related debt has grown rapidly, much of it channelled through complex and relatively opaque financing structures. Exposure to the theme is concentrated in a small number of companies, so a setback at a major player could spread. And high hedge fund leverage, combined with dealers' limited capacity to intermediate trades, could amplify any market stress.

Resilient system, live vulnerabilities

The same discussion carried a counterweight. Fed staff described the financial system as resilient, with banks holding strong balance sheets and ample access to liquidity, and household balance sheets offering some protection against severe shocks. Even so, some policymakers cautioned that vulnerabilities inside the banking sector can emerge quickly despite reassuring assessments, and officials questioned whether regulatory data fully captures institutions' true exposure.

That tension shaped a debate about tools. A few officials considered raising capital requirements for banks. Others stressed making sure lenders are ready to use the Fed's emergency discount window in a period of stress. Some discussed creating a dedicated asset-purchasing mechanism for financial stability risks — an idea Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has argued should come with a clearly defined framework and an exit strategy, so any holdings are sold once conditions normalise. Several policymakers, however, cautioned against using monetary policy itself to manage market disruptions. The Federal Reserve's Financial Stability Report page carries the Board's current assessment in full.

Rates: held in October, December in focus

The stability debate sat alongside an inflation argument that dominated the meeting. Officials kept the policy rate at 3.75%-4.00% in October, with only Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a quarter-point increase, Reuters reported. Prices have been rising at more than a 3% annual rate with little recent improvement, and almost all policymakers believed further rate increases could be necessary if the economy develops in line with their expectations.

The October meeting also opened a more detailed discussion of AI itself — the risk of over-investment in the technology set against the productivity gains it might deliver. The next test comes quickly: the Fed meets again on December 8-9, with investors anticipating a quarter-point increase and the minutes setting up a debate over whether a larger move, or tougher language, is needed.
